profiles.meeting_scenario: A weekly coordination meeting in an ML systems research lab between the lead author of an internal survey reproduction effort and the engineer preparing the shared benchmark stack for a companion artifact release. The team is turning the seed topic into a lab-internal benchmark package and slide deck comparing distributed training patterns for ResNet-50 on ImageNet across several cluster setups. The immediate context is that the writing workstream needs stable throughput numbers, setup notes, and run logs from the engineering workstream by the end of the week so the survey appendix and artifact checklist can be finalized. The agenda is to align on what runs are considered 'baseline' and 'scaling' runs, what exactly will be handed off in the benchmark bundle, which code branch and cluster environment the next batch of experiments should use, and how status will be tracked in the shared document. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on the benchmark handoff, run schedule, and ownership of the shared results folder, while several second-order assumptions remain unspoken.

members.name: Dr. Maya Chen
members.expertise: Distributed deep learning systems, benchmark design, empirical analysis for training throughput and convergence comparisons
members.background: Maya leads a small ML systems group at an industry research lab and is drafting an internal survey-style report plus artifact appendix on synchronous and asynchronous distributed SGD, all-reduce strategies, mixed precision, and large-batch training; she often works from summarized experiment tables rather than raw cluster operations details.
members.private_state: She wants a clean, publication-ready comparison table by Friday without reopening methodology debates, and she is especially concerned that inconsistent reporting formats will slow down the writing team more than any missing run.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'baseline run' for the report, they mean the single-node, 8-GPU DDP reference configuration already used in the draft tables.
A run counts as 'reproduced' once the expected throughput and top-1 trend are visible in the summary sheet, even if seed variance and full log packaging are still pending.
The 'benchmark bundle' naturally includes aggregated metrics tables, launch configs, and one representative log per setting, not every raw event file from every retry.

The shared results folder is effectively owned by the writing side once engineering drops in finalized summaries, so small renaming or reformatting for appendix consistency does not need separate coordination.

members.name: Alex Romero
members.role: Senior ML Systems Engineer and infrastructure coordinator
members.expertise: Multi-node training infrastructure, NCCL tuning, cluster scheduling, experiment automation, log collection, and artifact reproducibility
members.background: Alex maintains the lab's distributed training stack, including launcher scripts, Slurm templates, container images, and benchmark automation for ImageNet-scale experiments across 8 to 128 GPUs; he is responsible for making sure reported numbers can be rerun from the shared repository.
members.private_state: He wants to avoid last-minute ad hoc requests that force reruns or undocumented manual edits, and he is worried that the paper-oriented team will cite numbers from stale branches or partially complete runs.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'baseline run,' they mean the canonical reproducibility anchor: the current 32-GPU multi-node config on the artifact branch from which all scaling experiments inherit launcher settings.
A run is only 'reproduced' when the automation pipeline has completed, raw logs are archived, and the config can be relaunched without manual intervention.
The 'benchmark bundle' for handoff includes raw TensorBoard/event logs, environment manifests, launcher scripts, and retry history so downstream readers can audit anomalies.
The shared results folder remains owned by infrastructure until artifact freeze, so filenames, directory structure, and version tags should not be changed outside the automation pipeline.
References to 'the latest branch' naturally point to the artifact branch created after the AMP overflow fix last week.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the baseline run
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to 'the baseline' when planning the comparison table and next handoff.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the single-node 8-GPU ResNet-50 DDP reference setup already appearing in the survey draft as the anchor for scaling efficiency.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the canonical 32-GPU multi-node artifact configuration that the automation stack treats as the reproducibility anchor for all subsequent scaling runs.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both uses are legitimate in distributed training practice, and in a coordination meeting 'baseline' sounds like settled shared vocabulary, so neither expects it to require restatement.

misalignment_points.topic: What 'reproduced' means for a completed run
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both discuss whether certain results are 'reproduced' and ready to include.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks a setting is reproduced once the observed throughput and accuracy curve broadly match the expected trend well enough to populate tables and narrative claims.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks a setting is reproduced only when the full automated pipeline, archived logs, immutable config, and rerunnable scripts are all in place.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because both are aiming at reliability and quality, the phrase 'reproduced' carries a strong sense of agreement even though one applies a reporting threshold and the other an artifact threshold.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in the benchmark bundle
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Alex will hand off 'the benchmark bundle' for the appendix and shared folder.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the bundle contains the polished outputs needed by the writing workflow: summary CSVs, config snapshots, selected logs, and notes on anomalies.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the bundle contains the full reproducibility package: all raw logs, automation metadata, container/environment manifests, launch scripts, and retry traces.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like a natural project artifact with an obvious boundary, and both imagine their own standard package without needing to enumerate contents in a short status meeting.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree to use 'the latest branch' for the next round of runs and documentation updates.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the main research branch where the survey draft's current numbers were generated and where a few reporting-oriented script patches landed yesterday.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the artifact branch created after last week's AMP overflow fix and NCCL env cleanup, which he now treats as the operational default.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both branches are recent, both are internally called 'latest' in their respective workstreams, and the meeting context is coordination rather than code review, so the phrase passes without a commit hash or branch name.
